::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 17 [1899]  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown.  Printed in Coleridge, <i>[Life](other_books/otherbook_40.qmd)</i> p. 330
:::

[To [Marianne Bigg Wither](people/person_1546.qmd) about the death of her brother the Rev. [William Bigg Wither](people/person_1544.qmd).]

I had not heard for a fortnight, and had just made up my mind to write to ask [Raby](people/person_1221.qmd) whether you knew anything, and when I saw your writing I knew how it must be. This gradual, gentle sinking is the most merciful way of going one can think of, though I hope that there may not be the restlessness that belongs to weakness and is so very distressing. I shall ask [Henry Bowles](people/person_184.qmd) to pray for him, especially on Sunday when the people are there. I hope it is peaceful sleepiness, and that [your niece](people/person_1089.qmd) or one of the nephews can be with him. The last letter I had, now more than a fortnight ago, spoke of going to church at eleven and preaching from his chair.
